cards.front: What is an [[kw:inequality]]?
cards.back: A mathematical sentence that compares two expressions using <, >, ≤, or ≥. Example: $ x + 5 > 8 $.

cards.front: What does the symbol '≤' mean?
cards.back: [[imp:Less than or equal to]]. Key phrases: 'at most', 'no more than'.
[[imp:Greater than or equal to]]. Key phrases: 'at least', 'no less than'.
cards.front: What does the symbol '≥' mean?
Translate into an inequality: 'A number w minus 3.5 is less than or equal to −2'.
Translate into an inequality: 'Three is less than a number n plus 5'.
cards.back: $ 3 < n + 5 $, which is equivalent to $ n + 5 > 3 $.

cards.front: What is a [[kw:solution of an inequality]]?
cards.back: A value that makes the inequality true when substituted for the variable. An inequality can have many solutions.
The set of all solutions of an inequality. For $ x > 2 $, the solution set includes every number greater than 2.
cards.front: What is a [[kw:solution set]]?

cards.back: No. Substitute: $ -4 + 8 = 4 $, and $ 4 < -3 $ is false.
cards.front: Is −4 a solution of $ x + 8 < -3 $?
Is −4 a solution of $ -4.5x > -21 $?
cards.back: Yes. Substitute: $ -4.5(-4) = 18 $, and $ 18 > -21 $ is true.

cards.front: When graphing an inequality, when do you use an [[imp:open circle]]?
cards.back: For < or >, when the boundary number is [[imp:NOT part of the solution]].

cards.front: When do you use a [[imp:closed circle]] on a number line graph?
cards.back: For ≤ or ≥, when the boundary number [[imp:IS part of the solution]].

cards.front: Graph $ x > 2 $ on a number line.
cards.back: Open circle at 2, shade to the right.
Closed circle at -3, shade to the left.
cards.front: Graph $ y \le -3 $ on a number line.
Write an inequality from a graph: closed circle at 48, shading to the right.
A sign says 'Maximum Capacity: 600'. Write an inequality for the number of people p inside.
cards.back: $ p \le 600 $. 'Maximum' means at most 600.

cards.front: What are [[kw:equivalent inequalities]]?
cards.back: Inequalities that have the same solution set. They are produced by applying properties of inequality.
Adding the same number to each side produces an equivalent inequality. If $ a > b $, then $ a + c > b + c $.
cards.front: State the [[kw:Addition Property of Inequality]].
Solve $ x - 6 \ge -10 $ and graph.
cards.back: Add 6 to both sides: $ x \ge -4 $. Graph: closed circle at -4, shade right.
Subtracting the same number from each side produces an equivalent inequality. If $ a > b $, then $ a - c > b - c $.
cards.front: State the [[kw:Subtraction Property of Inequality]].

cards.back: Subtract 8 from both sides: $ y \le -3 $. Graph: closed circle at -3, shade left.
cards.front: Solve $ y + 8 \le 5 $ and graph.

cards.back: Subtract 1.4: $ -9.4 < m $. Rewrite: $ m > -9.4 $. Graph: open circle at -9.4, shade right.

cards.front: When solving $ k + 5 \le -3 $, what operation should you use?
cards.back: Subtract 5 from both sides (Subtraction Property of Inequality) to isolate $ k $.

cards.front: How do you check a solution of an inequality?
cards.back: [[imp:Substitute]] a value from the solution set into the original inequality. If true, it's correct. Test values around the boundary.

cards.front: Why simplify each side before solving an inequality?
cards.back: Combining like terms first makes the inequality [[imp:cleaner and easier to solve]], reducing potential errors.
Simplify left: $ j + 6 < 8 $. Subtract 6: $ j < 2 $. Graph: open circle at 2, shade left.
cards.front: Solve $ j + 9 - 3 < 8 $.
Solve $ 10 \ge 3p - 2p - 7 $.
cards.back: Combine like terms on right: $ 10 \ge p - 7 $. Add 7: $ 17 \ge p $, or $ p \le 17 $. Graph: closed at 17, shade left.

cards.front: A microwave uses 1100 W on a 1800 W circuit. Write and solve an inequality for additional watts $ w $.
cards.back: $ 1100 + w < 1800 $. Subtract 1100: $ w < 700 $. You can add less than 700 watts.
$ 38 + x \le 50 $. Subtract 38: $ x \le 12 $. You can add up to 12 pounds.
